rules.strength_selection: Each player selects one strength before missions are revealed.
rules.mission_selection: After strengths are locked, the group randomly selects one of six missions.
rules.gm_visibility: The game master reads the mission narration aloud. Players should not see the mission narration or GM notes in the player interface.
rules.card_flip: After the mission is selected, each player sees the front of their selected strength card. Tapping flips it to reveal the clue if one exists for that strength and mission.
rules.sharing: Players may share their clues and discuss a plan together.
rules.round_end: When discussion ends, the game master ends the round and players return to strength selection.
rules.clue_distribution: Each mission gives additional information to 13–17 of the 24 strengths (slightly more than half); remaining strengths have no mission-specific clue.

missions.title: The Broken Bridge
missions.gm_read_aloud: A deep ravine separates your party from the old watchtower. The stone bridge has collapsed in the middle. The water below is rising, and dark clouds suggest you do not have much time. Around the broken bridge are scattered supplies, strange markings, and several possible routes. Your whole party must reach the other side. How will you cross?
missions.gm_notes: Accept creative plans. The party needs a safe way across and a way to get everyone over. A good plan may use the bridge, build a crossing, find an alternate route, or combine approaches. Do not reveal clue details unless a player taps a strength card that has one.

strength_clues.Creativity: You spot a coil of rope, loose planks, a fallen flagpole and thick vines. The flagpole could work as a support beam, while the rope and vines could help secure a makeshift crossing.
strength_clues.Curiosity: You notice fresh scrape marks near a bridge support. Looking closer reveals a narrow maintenance ledge partly hidden beneath the bridge.
strength_clues.Judgment: The party has three broad options: repair the bridge, cross the remaining platforms, or take a longer path around the ravine. The repair is fastest if properly secured; the platforms are quicker but riskier; the detour is safer but costs time.
strength_clues.Love of Learning: An old builder's plaque describes a simple rope-and-counterweight bridge design. You recognise how the available rope and pole could be used to make a basic guide line.
strength_clues.Perspective: From a higher viewpoint, you can see a winding trail around the ravine. It takes longer but avoids the broken bridge entirely.
strength_clues.Bravery: A narrow ledge offers a daring shortcut to a stable anchor point on the far side. It is exposed, but reaching it could help secure a rope for everyone else.
strength_clues.Perseverance: The stone supports are damaged but not completely useless. With patient testing and repeated adjustments, the party may be able to stabilise one small section long enough for a careful crossing.
strength_clues.Social Intelligence: A nervous raven keeps circling one section of the cliff and avoids another. Its behaviour suggests something about the wind or loose stones nearby; observing it may help the party choose where to investigate.
strength_clues.Teamwork: The crossing will be much safer if one person checks the anchor, another secures the line, and the others cross one at a time while someone keeps the rope steady.
strength_clues.Fairness: The lightest or most agile member might cross first, but the plan must also account for anyone carrying equipment or needing extra support. A plan that only works for some of the party is not a complete solution.
strength_clues.Leadership: The group is losing time because everyone is suggesting a different route. A clear plan with assigned roles could prevent several people from taking the same risk at once.
strength_clues.Prudence: Two platforms that look sturdy have hairline cracks underneath. A small foothold hidden below the third platform offers a safer route if crossed slowly.
strength_clues.Hope: You spot a weathered trail marker on the far cliff. It suggests that people have crossed this ravine before, and there may be a workable route even if the bridge cannot be repaired.

missions.title: The Whispering Library
missions.gm_read_aloud: Deep inside a ruined library, a sealed door blocks the way to the next chamber. Three stone symbols glow above the lock, and whispers drift between towering shelves. Some books are chained shut, others lie scattered across the floor, and a cold wind moves through a room with no visible windows. The door must be opened without bringing the unstable library down. What will you do?
missions.gm_notes: The intended solution is to understand and activate the lock without damaging the room. Allow players to research, interpret symbols, listen, experiment carefully, or ask the library's spirit for help.

strength_clues.Creativity: Several objects could be combined into a tool: a mirror shard, a brass bookmark and a loose piece of wire. They might help redirect light or reach a recessed switch.
strength_clues.Curiosity: The whispers grow louder near one shelf, and one book is dust-free despite the rest being covered. Something there has been handled recently.
strength_clues.Judgment: The three symbols appear to represent moon, key and tree. The same three symbols appear in different orders in the room; compare the evidence before trying a sequence.
strength_clues.Love of Learning: You recognise the lock's symbols as an old indexing system. The order is likely based on a book classification rule rather than a spoken password.
strength_clues.Perspective: The symbols on the door are part of a larger mural that stretches across the ceiling. Looking at the entire mural reveals that the door is only one part of the puzzle.
strength_clues.Honesty: One whisper repeats a phrase that sounds persuasive but contradicts the inscription carved beside it. The inscription is fixed and appears more trustworthy than the changing voice.
strength_clues.Kindness: A small spectral librarian is trapped behind a fallen shelf. Helping it may earn its trust and provide guidance, though moving the shelf carelessly could damage nearby stacks.
strength_clues.Social Intelligence: The whispering spirit sounds frightened rather than hostile. Its tone changes when the party speaks gently and stops when someone shouts.
strength_clues.Teamwork: The lock has three symbols that must be pressed at nearly the same time. The party will need to coordinate rather than have one person rush between them.
strength_clues.Fairness: The shelves contain clues written in different scripts. Each member may recognise a different part; make sure everyone has a chance to contribute before deciding the answer.
strength_clues.Humility: The most obvious inscription may not be the important one. A smaller note tucked low on the shelf seems deliberately easy to overlook.
strength_clues.Prudence: The floor tiles nearest the door are cracked and may trigger a collapse if too much weight is placed on them. Test the room from the edges before approaching the lock.
strength_clues.Appreciation of Beauty and Excellence: The mural's decorative pattern contains repeated shapes that are too precise to be merely ornamental. Following the pattern may reveal the order of the symbols.

missions.title: The Village Without a Bell
missions.gm_read_aloud: A mountain village is preparing for its annual lantern festival, but the great bell that begins the ceremony has vanished. Without it, the villagers fear the festival cannot begin and the valley's old protective tradition will be broken. Several people are upset, rumours are spreading, and the sun is setting. Find out what happened and help the village decide what to do.
missions.gm_notes: This is a social investigation, not a combat encounter. The bell has been moved to protect it from a damaged tower; a young apprentice knows part of the truth but is afraid of being blamed. Players can solve the problem through listening, evidence, teamwork and a fair plan.

strength_clues.Creativity: The festival does not necessarily need the original bell to begin. You can imagine alternatives using lanterns, drums, chimes or a coordinated light signal.
strength_clues.Curiosity: You notice fresh cart tracks leading away from the bell tower and a smear of blue paint matching the village workshop.
strength_clues.Judgment: Three rumours blame different villagers, but only one account matches the timeline and physical evidence. Separate what is known from what people merely suspect.
strength_clues.Perspective: The tower has a new crack near its base. The bell may have been moved for a reason beyond theft, and the village's safety matters more than preserving the ceremony exactly as planned.
strength_clues.Bravery: The apprentice is being blamed publicly, but you can speak up and ask the villagers to pause their accusations until the facts are clear.
strength_clues.Honesty: One witness admits privately that they saw the bell being moved but has exaggerated the story to avoid looking careless. A calm, non-accusatory conversation may clarify what really happened.
strength_clues.Zest: The crowd's disappointment is spreading. A lively alternative celebration could help keep people engaged while the party investigates.
strength_clues.Love: You notice that the apprentice is more worried about disappointing the village than about being punished. Showing care may help them explain what they know.
strength_clues.Kindness: An elderly villager is overwhelmed by the rumours and needs help getting home. Offering support may also give the party a calmer chance to hear their recollection.
strength_clues.Social Intelligence: The workshop leader appears defensive when the tower is mentioned, while the apprentice keeps looking towards the damaged roof. Their reactions suggest the conversation should be handled sensitively.
strength_clues.Teamwork: The investigation will move faster if the party divides tasks: check the tower, speak with witnesses, follow the tracks, and examine the workshop.
strength_clues.Fairness: Several villagers are being accused without evidence. Give each person a chance to explain before deciding who is responsible.
strength_clues.Leadership: The villagers need a clear plan: pause the rumours, organise a search, and decide how to hold a safe festival if the bell cannot be returned in time.

missions.title: The Forest of Sleeping Roots
missions.gm_read_aloud: Your party enters a forest where the trees have become still and the roots curl across the path like sleeping serpents. A nearby settlement depends on this forest for clean water, but the stream has slowed to a trickle. Strange glowing spores drift in the air, and a stone marker stands beside a fork in the path. Discover what is disturbing the forest and find a way to restore the water.
missions.gm_notes: The cause is a blocked spring channel and a damaged root-stone that regulates the flow. The spores are a warning sign, not the main threat. The party can investigate, negotiate with forest creatures, repair the channel, or find a temporary water route.

strength_clues.Creativity: Nearby fallen branches, smooth stones and flexible vines could be used to redirect a small stream or clear a blocked channel without damaging the roots.
strength_clues.Curiosity: The glowing spores are denser near one path, but the damp soil and tiny insects point towards a different route. Following the small signs may lead to the spring.
strength_clues.Love of Learning: The stone marker uses an old symbol for water pressure. You recognise that the root-stone must be aligned with the channel rather than simply pulled out.
strength_clues.Perspective: The stream's blockage is only one part of the problem. The settlement needs a temporary water supply while the forest recovers, so the party should consider both immediate and longer-term needs.
strength_clues.Perseverance: The channel is clogged with layers of roots and silt. Clearing it will take patient work; pulling too hard could make the blockage worse.
strength_clues.Honesty: A trail of disturbed soil suggests someone has been digging here. The signs point to an attempt to divert water, rather than a natural failure alone.
strength_clues.Love: A young forest creature guards the spring because it fears the settlement will take all the water. A respectful approach may reveal why it is protecting the channel.
strength_clues.Kindness: A small animal is caught in the tangled roots near the stream. Freeing it safely could earn the forest creatures' trust.
strength_clues.Social Intelligence: The forest creatures react with alarm whenever tools strike the roots. They seem more willing to approach when the party slows down and avoids sudden movements.
strength_clues.Teamwork: The blockage has several parts: one person can clear silt, another stabilise the root-stone, and others can guide water into a temporary channel.
strength_clues.Forgiveness: The person who damaged the channel may have been trying to help their own village. Understanding their reason could make it easier to repair the damage and prevent it happening again.
strength_clues.Prudence: Some roots are load-bearing and must not be cut. A narrow section of the channel can be cleared safely, but the larger roots need to remain in place.
strength_clues.Appreciation of Beauty and Excellence: You notice that the healthy plants grow in a repeating pattern around small water vents. Following this pattern reveals where the original water channel runs beneath the forest floor.

missions.title: The Clockwork Keep
missions.gm_read_aloud: A clockwork keep has locked itself down, trapping a friendly messenger inside. Gears grind behind the walls, brass sentries patrol the hall, and a large countdown dial is moving towards zero. The main gate is sealed, but a maintenance panel, a narrow upper walkway and several control levers are visible. Get the messenger out before the keep completes its lockdown.
missions.gm_notes: The puzzle is about timing and coordination. The party can disable the mechanism, distract sentries, reach a control panel or find a maintenance route. Avoid requiring a single specific strength.

strength_clues.Creativity: A bent metal strip, a loose gear and a length of cord could be combined into a simple lever or tool to reach the maintenance latch.
strength_clues.Curiosity: The sentries repeat the same patrol route, but one pauses for a fraction longer near the western wall. You also hear a faint click behind the maintenance panel.
strength_clues.Judgment: The control levers affect different systems. The red lever appears to stop the gate but may activate the sentries; the blue lever slows the countdown; the brass lever seems to unlock the maintenance panel.
strength_clues.Love of Learning: The machine uses a familiar sequence of interlocking gears. You can infer that one gear must be held in place before the main lock can disengage.
strength_clues.Bravery: The upper walkway passes above the sentries and is exposed to moving gears. A careful but bold crossing could reach the emergency release.
strength_clues.Perseverance: The maintenance latch is jammed, but its mechanism is still moving. Repeated, measured attempts may loosen it without breaking the parts.
strength_clues.Honesty: The countdown dial is partly obscured by a cracked glass cover. Its markings show that the lockdown is triggered by the final bell, not by the dial reaching zero alone.
strength_clues.Zest: The sentries are attracted to sudden movement and sound. A fast, energetic distraction in the opposite corridor could create a brief opening.
strength_clues.Social Intelligence: The trapped messenger taps a repeating rhythm on the wall. It may be an attempt to communicate a pattern or indicate when the sentries pass.
strength_clues.Teamwork: Two controls must be held at once while another person operates the release. The party will need to assign roles and synchronise actions.
strength_clues.Leadership: The countdown is making everyone rush. A clear order of operations and named roles will reduce the chance of conflicting actions.
strength_clues.Humility: The main gate looks like the obvious route, but the upper walkway is marked for maintenance access and may be the intended path.
strength_clues.Prudence: The gears near the red lever are under tension. Pulling it immediately could cause a sudden movement; secure the smaller locking pin first.
strength_clues.Self-Regulation: The alarms and countdown are designed to provoke panic. Staying calm makes it easier to hear the gear rhythm and operate the controls precisely.

missions.title: The Trial of the Moon Gate
missions.gm_read_aloud: At the end of a long passage stands a moon-shaped gate. It will open only when the party completes an ancient trial. Three stone figures face a pool of silver water, and each holds a different object: a lantern, a bowl and a closed book. An inscription warns that force will seal the gate until dawn. The party must discover what the trial asks of them.
missions.gm_notes: The trial rewards cooperation, humility and meaning-making. The solution is to bring light to the pool, offer water to a thirsty stone creature, and read the book's final page together; each action represents insight, care and shared understanding. Other thoughtful solutions should be accepted.

strength_clues.Creativity: The lantern, bowl and book may be used in a way beyond their obvious purpose. You wonder whether their shadows, reflections or arrangement matter as much as the objects themselves.
strength_clues.Curiosity: The stone figures' eyes are angled towards the pool, not the gate. Tiny symbols around the water's edge suggest that the pool is central to the trial.
strength_clues.Judgment: The inscription warns against force, so attacking or prying at the gate is likely to make matters worse. Look for a solution consistent with the clues rather than testing brute strength.
strength_clues.Love of Learning: The inscription uses an old ceremonial phrase meaning 'share what illuminates, sustains and teaches.' You can connect this to the lantern, bowl and book.
strength_clues.Perspective: The three figures may represent parts of a community rather than separate riddles. The trial may require the party to understand how the objects work together.
strength_clues.Honesty: One line of the inscription is easy to misread as a command to sacrifice an object, but the original carving indicates that the objects should be offered temporarily, not destroyed.
strength_clues.Love: The stone creature beside the pool looks frightened and thirsty. Treating it as a participant rather than an obstacle may be important.
strength_clues.Kindness: The bowl is dry, and a small stone creature appears weakened. Offering it water may be one part of the trial.
strength_clues.Social Intelligence: The figures seem to respond to how the party interacts with one another. When players listen and build on each other's ideas, the moon symbols glow more brightly.
strength_clues.Teamwork: The trial's symbols are placed far apart, and the gate reacts only when several actions happen together. Coordinate the use of the lantern, bowl and book.
strength_clues.Fairness: The inscription includes the phrase 'no voice alone.' The trial may require each party member to contribute an idea or action rather than letting one person solve everything.
strength_clues.Forgiveness: A carved scene shows two figures turning away from one another before joining hands. The trial may involve repairing a relationship or choosing reconciliation over blame.
strength_clues.Humility: The final clue is carved near the floor, below eye level. Kneeling to examine it reveals that the trial is not about proving who is strongest.
strength_clues.Gratitude: A small inscription thanks those who tended the gate long ago. Expressing appreciation for the gifts represented by the three objects may be part of the ritual.
strength_clues.Hope: A faint line on the gate depicts a crescent becoming a full moon. The trial seems designed to reward patient progress; the first failed attempt does not mean the party has lost.
strength_clues.Humour: A tiny carving on the sternest stone figure shows it wearing a ridiculous little crown. A gentle joke or playful gesture may reveal that the trial is not meant to be approached with solemnity alone.
strength_clues.Spirituality: The pool reflects the night sky even though the ceiling is stone. The trial may ask the party to consider what connects them to something larger than individual success.
